Gently AI

Gently AI is building a ground-up AI-native enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform targeting the $50B+ legacy ERP market dominated by SAP and Oracle. Rather than retrofitting AI onto existing architectures, Gently rebuilds core financial and operational workflows from first principles using AI agents. Modules include Order Management, Rebates, Ship & Debit, Accounts Payable, and EDI Support — with two modules already live in production at Fortune 500 design partners. Eight Fortune 500 design partners are on board, and the December 2025 bridge was led by Khosla Ventures at a $70M post-money cap.

Even Platforms

Even Platforms is building a distributed network of modular, automated machine shops to address a critical vulnerability in the American industrial base. The company owns and operates standardized factories equipped with Okuma CNC machinery, Fastems robotics, and Mitutoyo CMM inspection, unified by a proprietary software intelligence layer ("EvenOS") that compounds operational knowledge across every factory in the network. The $50B U.S. machined-parts market is structurally fragmented, labor-constrained — 25% of the manufacturing workforce will retire by 2030 — and undersupplied as defense spending and reshoring demand accelerate. Factory 1 in Dallas-Fort Worth was stood up in 10 days and began shipping parts in May 2026. XPV led the $6M seed round alongside Pear VC.

Piris Labs

Piris Labs builds pluggable optical transceivers optimized specifically for AI inference workloads — addressing the "98% problem," the architectural reality that as AI models scale across distributed clusters, the bandwidth required to move training and inference data exceeds compute throughput, making the networking layer (not raw GPU FLOPS) the binding constraint. The flagship Pi Engine targets 1.6 Tbps baseline performance with a 3.2 Tbps roadmap and is differentiated from incumbents like Lightmatter (which builds optical switches) by its inference-specific optimization and GPU- and software-agnostic pluggable form factor.

Starcloud

Starcloud is building data centers in space — megawatt-scale orbital infrastructure scalable to gigawatt capacity, designed to solve the energy and cooling constraints that increasingly bind AI compute on Earth. The company is a Y Combinator S24 graduate headquartered in Redmond, Washington. In November 2025 Starcloud launched Starcloud-1, the first satellite to carry an NVIDIA H100 GPU, and successfully trained NanoGPT in orbit — the first LLM ever trained in space. In March 2026 the company filed an FCC application for an 88,000-satellite orbital data center constellation and reached a $1.1B valuation just 17 months out of YC, the fastest YC unicorn on record. XPV's Series A+ follow-on closed at the same time. Existing backers include Y Combinator, NFX, In-Q-Tel, and NVIDIA's Inception program.

Neotix

Neotix is building a vertically integrated teleoperation and data infrastructure layer for embodied AI. The company operates large-scale teleoperation centers in Rwanda to provide robotics training data, annotation services, and model evaluation at $30/hour with 61% gross margins—delivering 5x more training data at 70% lower cost than US alternatives. Their "leased environments" strategy allows delivery on customer contracts while building custom "Hollywood set" style environments simulating Western commercial spaces.

Egra AI

Egra AI is building a general-purpose foundation model for EEG— effectively "GPT for brain signals." The company aggregates clinical- grade EEG data through exclusive hospital and device manufacturer partnerships to train a self-supervised model that generalizes across subjects and hardware, monetizing via API/licensing. Target applications span clinical diagnostics (seizure prediction, Alzheimer's biomarkers), cognitive monitoring, and ultimately silent thought-to-text interfaces for consumer BCIs.
